decisions.quote:
Our results suggest that the original findings of a facial feedback
effect (Strack et al., 1988) and the null effect in the replication studies
(Wagenmakers et al., 2016) are not contradictory: The facial-feedback
effect was present when the camera was absent and participants were
not concerned with performance monitoring; The effect diminished
when the participants’ performance was recorded and participants
were warned that their performance was being monitored.
decisions.reason: The no-camera condition directly repeats the procedure of Strack et al. (1988) and confirms a significant facial-feedback effect, while the camera-present condition repeats the modified procedure of Wagenmakers et al. (2016); the authors' overall verdict is that the original finding by Strack et al. (1988) is correct and replicated when tested under its unmonitored procedure.

decisions.quote:
However, in the present work we sought
to compare the outcomes of the two specific procedures that were
used in past studies, one by Strack et al. (1988) and the other by
Wagenmakers et al. (2016), and therefore, we repeated the same
procedures that were used in those studies.
decisions.reason: Omitted target: the paper explicitly repeats the camera-present procedure of Wagenmakers et al. (2016) to re-test its reported null finding and confirms the absence of the facial-feedback effect when a camera is present.
